headline.text: Asked for trade-offs in planning, but only pass/fail for a test

observations.text: In project planning, the user asked to see alternatives and what would be given up before deciding. On a routine test result, the user asked only whether it passed.
For a high-risk migration, the user asked for the failure cases and a way back before approving.
In a separate record, the user said they do not always want short answers. They want enough to judge what to do.

interpretation.text: In these records, the user asked for more when a decision or approval was ahead, and for less when a result was routine. Their own words in J5 fit this: enough to judge, not a fixed length.

alternative: The difference may come from the topic itself, such as migrations needing rollback details by project rule, and not from whether a decision was ahead. Other factors we cannot see may also play a part.
limitation: We do not know why the user made each request, or whether J2 involved any decision. J4 gives no exact words and no link to J3, so it cannot show how these requests relate.
